Bernstein: SEC and CFTC May Accelerate Rulemaking After CLARITY Act Stalls Bernstein analysts expect the SEC and CFTC to accelerate rules on token taxonomy, DeFi and self-custody protections, equity tokenization, real-world asset perpetual futures and sports event contracts. They said a CLARITY Act re-vote is unlikely due to limited time and concerns over its ethics provisions. — link

Circle Launches Arc Mainnet with BlackRock and Visa as Validators, Mints 10 Billion ARC Tokens Circle has launched the public mainnet of Arc, an open Layer 1 blockchain for financial markets and agentic activity. More than 100 applications and 100+ institutions and ecosystem builders are live at launch. Founding validators include BlackRock, DTCC, Galaxy, ICE, Mastercard, SBI Group, Standard Chartered and Visa. Arc uses USDC for gas and offers sub-second finality. Circle also completed the genesis mint of 10 billion ARC tokens but said this does not commit it to a public token launch. — link

U.S. House to Consider Crypto Tax and Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bills Today According to Eleanor Terrett, although the Clarity Act may be stalled in the Senate, the House will continue considering crypto-related legislation today. At 10:00 a.m. ET, the House Ways and Means Committee will mark up a crypto tax bill, while the House Financial Services Committee will begin considering several bills, including the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve bill introduced by Rep. Nick Begich earlier this year. — link

CFTC Chairman Michael Selig: Agency Will Advance Crypto Rules Under Existing Statutory Authority U.S. CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said on X that yesterday’s Senate vote was unfortunate and that Americans deserve regulatory clarity, legal certainty and consumer protections in crypto asset markets. He said President Trump had promised to deliver a future-proof crypto asset regulatory market structure, adding that the CFTC would help advance it using its existing statutory authority. Selig added that the CFTC is ready to issue rules for the “new frontier of finance.” — link
